subject: Chemistry
title: Name and Classify Haloalkanes: NCERT Questions Solved
summary: Three NCERT exercise questions solved with one checklist: longest chain (look inside the branches), lowest locants, alphabetical order on a tie; and the class (1°, 2°, 3°) is decided only by the carbon that carries the halogen. CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₂I is 1-iodo-2,2-dimethylbutane (1°), CH₃C(Cl)(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃ is 3-chloro-3-methylpentane (3°), and CH₃CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH₃ is 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane.

notes.title: 05 – Name and Classify Haloalkanes: NCERT Questions

keyPoints: **Checklist**: longest chain → **lowest locants** → **alphabetical order** only on a tie.
**Class** (1°, 2°, 3°) depends only on the **carbon carrying X**: how many carbons it is bonded to.
CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₂I = **1-iodo-2,2-dimethylbutane**, a **primary** alkyl halide (NCERT Ex 6.1 iii).
CH₃C(Cl)(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃ = **3-chloro-3-methylpentane**, **tertiary**: the chain runs through C₂H₅ (Ex 6.1 vii).
CH₃CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH₃ = **2-bromo-3-chlorobutane**: {2,3} both ways, **B before C** (Ex 6.2 i).

sections.h: The three questions in the video

list: Treating C₂H₅ as only a branch: the longest chain can run through it.
Judging 1°/2°/3° from the crowded neighbour carbon instead of the C–X carbon.
Using alphabetical order before the lowest-locant rule: it only breaks a tie.

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2C(CH3)2CH2I is:
quiz.explain: From the I end the locants are 1, 2, 2 (iodo on C1, two methyls on C2), lower than 4, 3, 3.
The C–I carbon (CH₂) is bonded to one carbon; the crowded neighbour does not decide.

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of CH3C(Cl)(C2H5)CH2CH3 is:
quiz.explain: The longest chain runs through the ethyl group (5 C, pentane); Cl and CH₃ both sit on C3, chloro written first.
The C–Cl carbon is bonded to three carbons.

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH3 is:
quiz.explain: Both ends give {2,3}: a tie, so bromo (B before C) gets 2.

quiz.q: When both numbering directions give the same locants, the lower number goes to the substituent that:
quiz.explain: Alphabetical order breaks a tie of locants.

quiz.q: To decide 1°, 2° or 3°, you look at:
options: the carbon next to the halogen-bearing carbon
the carbon that carries the halogen
quiz.explain: Only the carbon carrying X is counted.
It has two halogen atoms (Cl and Br).

quiz.q: In CH3C(Cl)(C2H5)CH2CH3 the longest chain has:

quiz.explain: The C–Cl carbon is bonded to three CH₃ groups.

simulation.reason: Practice questions on fixed structures; no continuous variable to explore, and the video works each solution.
